mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series 216i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement B38 engine for the BMW 2 Series 216i typically costs £1,100-£2,600 supply-only, depending on condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt). With fitting, expect £1,900-£3,800 total. Used engine: £1,100-£1,500. Reconditioned engine: £1,500-£2,000. Rebuilt engine: £2,000-£2,600.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine mount failure in a BMW 2 Series 216i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include excessive cabin vibrations at idle, a clunking noise when shifting from Drive to Reverse, and a generally rough feel from the engine. Often caused by fluid leaking from the mounts. Can be diagnosed by a visual inspection. Replacing all three mounts as a set is the recommended fix.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series 216i?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a typical used value of £5,000-£10,000, engine replacement is financially viable for most 216i owners - especially if the car is otherwise in good condition with a full service history. Rebuilt engine cost: £2,000-£2,600 (supply only). Adds years of reliable service with upgraded components. 12-month warranty provides peace of mind.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series 216i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series 216i engine replacement takes 2-3 working days for supply-only delivery, and an additional 1-2 days for fitting by a specialist workshop. Supply-only: 2-3 working days for UK delivery. Supply & fit: 3-5 working days total. Always confirm timelines with your chosen supplier.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 216i and the 218i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both use the same B38 1.5-litre three-cylinder petrol engine, but the 218i is tuned to a higher output - typically 136hp (100kW) compared to the 216i's 102-109hp (75-80kW). Same engine block and displacement. Different ECU calibration. 216i: 102-109hp; 218i: 136hp.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement BMW 2 Series 216i engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 2 Series 216i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Parts and labour covered (terms vary by supplier). Warranty is transferable if you sell the vehicle. Always confirm exact warranty terms before purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series 216i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 216i was introduced in March 2015 as an entry-level petrol option for the 2 Series Active Tourer (F45), BMW's first front-wheel-drive MPV. It was later joined by the 2 Series Gran Tourer (F46) in July 2015, offering the same 1.5-litre three-cylinder petrol engine in a seven-seat body. The 216i badge also appeared on the F44 Gran Coupe from 2022 onwards, though this was a different generation with a higher-output tune of the same B38 engine.

milestones.description: March 2015 - B38A15U0, 1.5L 3-cylinder petrol, 102hp (75kW), introduced in the Active Tourer (F45)
July 2015 - B38A15U0, 1.5L 3-cylinder petrol, 102hp (75kW), introduced in the Gran Tourer (F46)
2018 - B38A15U0 produced for UK market across both F45 and F46 body styles
216i badge temporarily discontinued from UK line-up
216i badge reintroduced on F44 Gran Coupe with B38A15U1, 109hp (80kW)

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series 216i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3: The B38 1.5-litre three-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the BMW 2 Series 216i is generally regarded as one of BMW's more reliable modern petrol engines. Early concerns about three-cylinder refinement and longevity have largely faded as higher-mileage examples continue to perform without major internal failures. However, a handful of well-documented weak points exist - engine mount wear, turbocharger seal failure, and coolant system issues are the most common drivers of repair enquiries. Rebuilt BMW 2 Series 216i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Engine Mount Wear - Why the BMW 2 Series 216i B38 Suffers from Vibration Issues
problems.rootCause: The engine mounts on the B38 contain fluid-filled damping chambers that can crack and leak over time. When the fluid escapes, the mounts lose their vibration-damping capability, transmitting engine harshness into the cabin. This is particularly noticeable at idle and during gear changes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the failed mount only
repairOptions.longevity: Short-term fix; other mounts may fail later

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of all three engine and transmission mounts
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended; addresses all mounts at once, prevents recurrence

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt B38 with new mounts and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if the engine has suffered catastrophic damage from another cause

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 2 Series 216i (2015-2018) with average mileage is worth approximately £5,000-£10,000 depending on condition, service history, and body style [THIRD-PARTY]. This places it in the £5,000-£8,000 band: evaluate both repair and replacement options. A full mount replacement set is almost always the economically sensible route.
problems.recommendation: Engine mount wear on the BMW 2 Series 216i is a maintenance item, not a reason for engine replacement. Replace all three mounts as a set for the best long-term result. Full engine replacement is not warranted for mount issues alone.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW 2 Series 216i engine mount repair costs

problems.h4: Turbocharger Seal Failure - BMW 2 Series 216i B38 Turbo Issues
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger seals on the B38 can fail over time, allowing oil to pass into the intake or exhaust system. Symptoms include a check engine light, noticeable power loss under load, light blue smoke at hard throttle, and a whistling noise from the turbo area.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Visual inspection and diagnostic fault code reading
repairOptions.longevity: First step to confirm turbo seal failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip, inspect, and rebuild the existing turbo with new seals and bearings
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the turbo core is in good condition

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement with a new or reconditioned OEM-spec turbocharger
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if the turbo has suffered significant wear or damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt B38 with new turbo and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if turbo failure has caused internal engine damage - rare on the B38

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a BMW 2 Series 216i worth £5,000-£10,000, turbocharger replacement (£900-£1,400 specialist) is a worthwhile investment. Full engine replacement is rarely necessary for turbo issues alone.
problems.recommendation: If you experience power loss or see blue smoke from your BMW 2 Series 216i, have the turbo inspected immediately. Catching seal failure early allows for a rebuild or replacement of the turbo alone. Ignoring the symptoms can lead to oil starvation and engine damage - at which point a rebuilt engine becomes the only viable option.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW 2 Series 216i turbocharger repair costs

problems.h4: Cooling System Issues - Thermostat & Water Pump Failure
problems.rootCause: The thermostat on the B38 can stick closed, preventing proper coolant flow and causing the engine to run hot. Symptoms include the temperature gauge creeping toward the hot zone in traffic, with no visible coolant leaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the thermostat and coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Standard repair for cooling system issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the water pump and coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: If water pump is also failing or as preventative maintenance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt B38
repairOptions.longevity: Only if overheating has caused head gasket or internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Thermostat or water pump replacement is a fraction of the cost of engine replacement and is almost always the right choice for a BMW 2 Series 216i.
problems.recommendation: Cooling system issues on the BMW 2 Series 216i are straightforward to fix. If you notice the temperature gauge climbing, have the thermostat and water pump inspected immediately. Continued driving with an overheating engine can cause head gasket failure or warped cylinder head - at which point a rebuilt engine becomes the only sensible option.
